info.title: waypoint API
info.description:
A task tracker with dependency and status management. A task depends on other tasks, and the service keeps it from being started while it is blocked by one still open, or finished before its acceptance criteria are met.

- `status` is one of `backlog`, `in_progress`, `review`, `done` or `cancelled`. `done` and `cancelled` are the closed statuses.
- A task **depends on** other tasks, and is **ready** when it is in `backlog` and every task it depends on is closed.
- A task can move to `in_progress`, `review` or `done` once every task it depends on is closed, and to `done` once every criterion is met and every subtask is closed.
- A task's **subtasks** are the steps of its work, with dependencies among themselves held to the same rule. Its **criteria** are what must be true for it to be done.
- A task's **verification** says who checks that its work does what it should, `agent` or `person`, and when, `before_release` or `after_release`; null if no one has said.
- Cancelled tasks count as closed, and `ListTasks` leaves them out unless `includeCancelled` is `true` or `status` is `cancelled`.

Every request takes `Authorization: Bearer <token>` but these, which hold no data: `GetHealth` (`/health`), the contracts (`/openapi.json`, `/mcp.json`), the docs (`/docs/api`, `/docs/mcp`) and the page (`/`, `/ui/…`). A write is recorded as its `x-actor` header, else its token's name; one by the environment's admin token (`WAYPOINT_ADMIN_TOKEN`), which has no name, as null.

The API's version, 2026-11-14, is the date its contract last changed, as AWS dates theirs; the package's version is apart, and `GetHealth` gives it. Errors are `{code, message}`.

shortId.description: The shortest prefix of `id`, at least 8 characters, that no other task's ID starts with. Accepted wherever an ID is.

title.description: A short name for the task.

description.description: What the task is, in Markdown.

status.description: Where it stands. `done` and `cancelled` are the closed statuses.

dependsOn.description: The IDs of the tasks this one depends on.

subtasks.description: The steps of the work, in order. The task can't be `done` until each is closed.

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria, in order. The task can't be `done` until each is met.

assignee.description: Who the task is assigned to, as free text; null if no one.

by.description: Who checks the work does what it should: `agent`, the one doing the work, or `person`, the person it is for.

when.description: When they check it: `before_release`, before the work reaches its users, or `after_release`, once it has.

verification.description: Who checks the task's work and when; null if no one has said.

updatedAt.description: When, as an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC.

blockedBy.description: The tasks in `dependsOn` that aren't closed yet.
